title: Conditional dependence and Scrooge ensembles in shallow random quantum circuits
authors: Yinchen Liu, Max McGinley, Thomas Schuster, David Gosset
abstract: The output state of a 2D geometrically local shallow random quantum circuit does not have long range correlations due to its lightcone structure. But this changes if one measures a subset of the qubits: long-range entanglement can be induced by the measurement process, leading to conditional correlations between distant qubits. In this paper we investigate the structure of conditional dependence in these circuits and its consequences for quantum advantage. For a tripartition $ABC$ of the qubits, we consider the ensemble of post-measurement states on $A$ that is conditioned on a specific measurement outcome on $B$ and ranges over all possible measurement outcomes on $C$. For circuit depths exceeding a constant critical value $d^*$, we conjecture that this ensemble is well approximated by a certain generalization of the Haar ensemble, called the Scrooge ensemble~[Jozsa \textit{et al.}, \href{https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.49.668}{Phys. Rev. A \textbf{49}, 668 (1994)}]; we also provide supporting numerical and analytical evidence. Our conjecture describes a precise sense in which the state retains its lightcone structure on the remaining unmeasured qubits, but also develops some globally random features arising from the measurement. A consequence is that $n$-qubit shallow random quantum circuits in two dimensions are classically efficiently simulable in the presence of a tiny depolarizing noise rate $Ω(\log(n)/n)$.
summary: This work analyzes how measuring subsets of qubits in shallow random quantum circuits induces long-range entanglement, leading to conditional dependencies. The authors conjecture that these post-measurement states follow a 'Scrooge ensemble,' which mathematically implies that the complex quantum dynamics are efficiently simulable classically, even when noise is present.
main_problem: The paper investigates the structure of conditional dependence induced by measurements on qubits within shallow random quantum circuits (SRQCs) and how this relates to classical simulation complexity.
main_result: For sufficiently deep SRQCs, the post-measurement state ensemble is conjectured to be approximated by a 'Scrooge ensemble,' leading to the conclusion that these circuits are classically efficiently simulable even with small depolarizing noise.
method: The analysis uses theoretical conjectures (the Scrooge hypothesis) and rigorous mathematical tools like analyzing moment matching via Diagonal Frame Potentials (DFP) to bound the relative error between the actual post-measurement ensemble and the predicted Haar/Scrooge measure.
model_or_system: The model is an n-qubit two-dimensional lattice subjected to shallow random quantum circuits (SRQCs) with nearest-neighbor gates, partitioned into three regions A, B, and C for measurement analysis.
key_observables: Conditional Mutual Information $I(A; C|B)$, the relative error between moment expectations of the actual ensemble vs. the Scrooge ensemble ($\epsilon$), and the Diagonal Frame Potential (DFP).
important_parameters: Circuit depth ($d > d^* = \Theta(1)$), system size ($n$), and the width parameter $	ext{width}(B) = 	ext{dist}(A, C) - 1$.
main_assumptions: The core conjecture is that the post-measurement ensemble approximates the Scrooge ensemble; further analysis relies on assuming stabilizer state structures for bounding errors.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate numerical evidence showing non-zero conditional mutual information at sufficient depth, and plots demonstrate that the average relative error decays inverse exponentially with the separation width between measured regions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical phenomenon of measurement-induced long-range entanglement to formulating the Scrooge ensemble conjecture. It then develops rigorous mathematical machinery using moment matching (DFP) to prove the convergence of observables towards this idealized, classically simulable limit.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete mechanism by which local quantum dynamics can generate non-local correlations that are nevertheless efficiently simulated classically due to underlying structural constraints revealed by measurement theory.
